error_model.logging: Pass-through to underlying logger; SafeLogger itself does not log errors.
raises: TypeError when logger is not a logging.Logger or IChannelLogger
ValueError when level_name is not a supported level

side_effects: emits log calls on the underlying logger

review_triggers: Any change to channel vs stdlib branching
Any change to method signature or defaults
safe_changes: Add new helpers that delegate to _emit without changing signatures
Add new metadata pass-through fields with defaults

runtime_couplings: Relies on IChannelLogger.mask_log for masked emissions
Relies on logging.Logger for stdlib fallback

dependents.notes: SafeLogger is the default adapter for repo logging; treat signature changes as breaking.

integration_flow: Emit structured error with method name and metadata

order_constraints: cleanup underlying logger before nulling references

lifecycle.construction: Instantiate with an optional logger; sets the logger level when provided.
lifecycle.ownership: Owns a reference to the logger but does not manage logger lifetime beyond optional cleanup.

invariants: If _logger is None, emitters return without side effects
Channel logging path always uses _manual_stack and _method_name
non_goals: No IO beyond emitting log calls
No policy decisions about message content
pitfalls: Assuming mask applies to stdlib logging
responsibilities: Provide a single logging API for ChannelLogger and stdlib loggers
Preserve method_name and manual stack metadata for channel logs
Keep stdlib logging as a secondary fallback

summary.detail: Provides a unified logging surface with masking support for channel loggers and a safe stdlib fallback. It never emits when no logger is configured and avoids mutating caller state.
summary.one_liner: SafeLogger adapts IrisLogger/ChannelLogger and stdlib logging into one contract.

coverage_expectations: Channel logger path uses mask_log with metadata

symbols.docstring: Unified logger adapter for channel and stdlib loggers.

symbols.docstring: Internal: route to ChannelLogger or stdlib logger.
